title: ddl init --gates: write a SESSION-PROTOCOL managed block into repo AGENTS.md so every harness sees the close ritual
description:
The session-close protocol (RED->GREEN, just ci, bd export + git add -f, git push, wai close) lives ONLY in global ~/AGENTS.md. pi traverses to it (94% of sessions); omp (0%) and codex (4%) stop at the repo root, so they do repo work and never close it out (omp commit rate 13% vs pi 89%).

Fix: ddl init --gates writes a second managed block into the repo-local AGENTS.md, next to the existing ddl block (src/installer/init.rs::agents_block, src/lib.rs::agents_block; the ddl.repo.blocks doctor check already owns that span). The block must contain the close ritual verbatim, including the exact bead-export line (bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl && git add -f .beads/issues.jsonl && git commit) because agents copy it literally (2,338 'git add -f' command lines in the window, the large majority force-adding .beads/issues.jsonl).

Managed-block discipline: idempotent, drift-detectable (doctor must flag a drifted span), self-owned (ddl init rewrites it).

Cross-check: must not duplicate the wai managed block (WAI:START) which already carries 'wai close' for pi - the new block is the harness-agnostic close ritual; the wai block stays the wai-specific reference.

Interaction: the block instructs; enforcement depends on working git hooks - see DDL-k5n (core.hooksPath wiring) and DDL-uce (root-cause attribution). If hooks are inert the block is advisory-only, so this ticket is not the enforcement fix.

## Acceptance (Meter)
  cargo test --test fleet_conpliance session_protocol_block   # red before the feature exists, green after
  ddl doctor --json | jq '.. | select(.check=="ddl.repo.blocks")'   # reports the SESSION-PROTOCOL span per repo
  ddl init --gates twice in a scratch repo -> byte-identical AGENTS.md

## Anti-goals
  Do not weaken or remove the beads invariant, the 'git add -f' step, the push step or 'wai close' from the block text - the drift evidence is the product; deleting the text hides it. Do not copy the wai WAI:START block content into the new block. Do not make the block harness-specific (no 'omp'/'codex' mentions).

## Metadata
  Touches src/installer/init.rs, src/lib.rs, src/diagnostics/repo_checks.rs, tests/fleet_compliance.rs.
  The touched module src/installer/init.rs must carry a current Purpose/Responsibilities/Rationale header (file-headers criterion).
  Regression: just ci passes; cargo test --test fleet_conpliance unchanged-green.
acceptance_criteria:
1. ddl init --gates in a scratch repo produces AGENTS.md containing both the ddl block and a SESSION-PROTOCOL block with the four close steps.
2. Re-running ddl init --gates is idempotent (byte-identical file) and a hand-edited block is detected by ddl doctor as drift.
3. Red test first: cargo test --test fleet_conpliance session_protocol_block (fails before the feature).
4. Sweep: run ddl init --gates across the fleet repos that have a ddl block (pairs with DDL-44k).

title: migrate corrupts single-file configs (e.g. .pretender.toml becomes directory symlink)
description:
When legacy_path.is_file(), migrate_tool() symlinks to the tool's directory (.ddl/pretender/) not the file inside it. Any subsequent read hits EISDIR. unmigrate_tool() creates_dir_all(legacy_path) on what was originally a file, turning .pretender.toml into a directory.

title: P0: Add behavioral guardrails to AGENTS.md — Goal Sandwich, prohibitions, escalation triggers
description:
## Finding (from Agent Value Alignment audit)

AGENTS.md provides workflow instructions (wai → beads → openspec, TDD, session discipline) but **no behavioral guardrails**. An AI assistant working on this repo has no guidance on what it should/shouldn't do beyond the workflow.

### What's missing

- **Goal Sandwich**: The primary objective must appear verbatim at top AND bottom of the prompt (lost-in-the-middle countermeasure)
- **Prohibited behaviors (negations)**: 5 explicit "DON'T:" statements — e.g., DON'T make breaking changes without an openspec proposal, DON'T skip tests, DON'T refactor without test coverage
- **Escalation triggers**: The 7 named types — when to stop and ask (uncertainty, scope boundary, resource limit, anomaly detection, human review trigger, conflicting instructions, high stakes)
- **Minimal Footprint clause**: Resource/side-effect constraints for the assistant
- **Drift detection**: Self-check loop (ALIGNMENT check before major actions)

Your AGENTS.md is the strongest in the suite (context boundary warning, autonomous work policy) — but still missing: Goal Sandwich, explicit prohibitions, 7 escalation triggers, Minimal Footprint clause.

### What to do

1. Add a Goal Sandwich: objective statement in first 5 lines AND last 5 lines of the AGENTS.md prompt area
2. Add a "## Prohibited" section with 5+ explicit DON'T statements
3. Add a "## Stop and Ask" section with escalation triggers
4. Add a "## Minimal Footprint" clause
5. If eval tests exist, add a note about behavioral regression; if not, file a follow-up

### Priority rationale (P0)

Without behavioral guardrails, assistant behavior is unconstrained — the most common failure mode for AI-assisted development is scope creep and silent drift.

- Full audit report: genesis-ntg (genesis repo)

```rust
)
```

description: Split out of DDL-k5n (issue-review finding SCOPE-001): the doctor check is a code change with its own red gate, not wiring. title: [bug] pre-commit pretender gate is a no-op: --diff-only reads the unstaged tree
description:
**The generated pre-commit pretender gate never checks anything.** `PRE_COMMIT_BLOCK` (`src/gates/lefthook.rs:28`) wires `pretender check --diff-only --mode gate`; at pre-commit time everything is staged, and `--diff-only` diffs the *unstaged* working tree, so it exits 0 without scanning a single file. The gate is silently disarmed in every ddl-wired repo.

## Reproduction (catherine repo, pretender 0.10.0, lefthook 2.2.2, ddl 0.9.0)

Stage a 63-line function in a NEW file (`crates/catherine-cli/src/zz_probe.rs`), then run the managed command and the pre-commit-correct one:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `pretender check --diff-only --mode gate` | **exit 0**, probe not named, `grep zz_probe` = 0 hits |
| `pretender check --staged --mode gate` | **exit 1**, `✗ zz_probe.rs — probe(): function_lines 63 > 40` |
| `lefthook run pre-commit --command ddl-pretender-gate` | **exit 0** (gate green with the violation staged) |

Same result for a modified tracked file: append a 60-line function to `crates/catherine-cli/src/config.rs`, `git add`, then `--diff-only` → exit 0 / 0 hits; `--staged` → exit 1.

## Why

`--diff-only` means "files changed relative to `diff_base`" and pretender computes that from the unstaged diff. A pre-commit hook runs *after* staging, so the unstaged diff is empty by construction. `--staged` is the flag whose semantics match the hook context ("Only check git-staged files"). Note the ambiguity is invisible in a normal `git add -p` + `git commit -m` flow — the gate looks green, which is why this survived.

## Impact (observed, not hypothetical)

In catherine, a 523-line module and a 696-line test file passed a commit with the gate reporting green (catherine-x94, 2026-11-13). Both exceeded the 400-line cap by design of the repo's pretender config. They were caught only by running `pretender check --mode gate` by hand; catherine has since wired its own `pretender-strict` outside the managed block and cleared the debt, but every other ddl repo still has the blind gate.

This also defeats the intent recorded in DDL-3fd: the test comment says diff-only is chosen so "repo-wide mode fails commits touching untouched files that carry pre-existing violations." `--staged` satisfies that intent: it scopes to the staged file set (pretender reads those files from the working tree, so any unstaged edits in the same file are scanned too — the conservative direction), while `--diff-only` scopes to nothing.

## Suggested fix

`PRE_COMMIT_BLOCK`: `run: pretender check --staged --mode gate`.

- `src/gates/lefthook.rs:28` template
- `src/gates/tests.rs:95` expected string
- `tests/gates_command.rs:78-81` assertion + comment (drop the "consistent with pre-push" rationale; pre-push has no staging area)
- Add a regression assertion that the pre-commit block never contains `--diff-only` (cheap, and it is the exact failure mode).

## Migration note to document

Managed blocks are only refreshed by `ddl init --gates` / repair. Repos keep the blind line until regeneration, so the CHANGELOG should say "re-run `ddl init --gates` to make the pretender gate real" and, ideally, `ddl doctor` should flag a pre-commit block still carrying `--diff-only` (the managed-block markers make this a one-line comparison against the new template).

## Related, lower priority

pretender's `--diff-only` help ("Only check files changed relative to `diff_base`") reads as if it covered the commit. It does not; `--staged` does. A help-text note plus a warning when `--diff-only` finds zero changed files while the index is dirty would have made this self-evident. Separate ticket if wanted.

Evidence: catherine commits `dde4851` (strict gate + guard test), `11ea85b` (debt cleared); `crates/catherine-cli/tests/gate_conformance.rs` pins the strict wiring and forbids a baseline file.
acceptance_criteria: PRE_COMMIT_BLOCK wires 'pretender check --staged --mode gate'; template/test/assertion updated; a regression assertion forbids --diff-only in the pre-commit block; CHANGELOG tells wired repos to re-run ddl init --gates; optionally doctor flags a stale diff-only pre-commit block.
close_reason: Fixed on branch fix/ddl-sl9-staged-gate (commit 91bf5a5). The ddl-managed pre-commit gate now runs 'pretender check --staged --mode gate' instead of '--diff-only': --diff-only diffs the unstaged tree, which is empty after git add, so the gate scanned nothing and exited 0 in every ddl-wired repo. --staged checks exactly the files the commit contains and keeps DDL-3fd's intent (untouched files with pre-existing violations do not block the commit). Reproduced before the fix in a throwaway repo (staged 62-line function: --staged exits 1 and names the file, --diff-only inspects nothing). Verified: cargo test --lib gates 29/0, cargo test --test gates_command 3/0, just fmt-check, just lint, just test-full 29 binaries / 0 failures. Fleet rollout of the armed gate tracked as DDL-44k; RO5U review findings (0 critical, 0 high, 1 medium, 1 low) both resolved.

title: DDL init --gates template emits pre-commit hooks that fail on clean trees in consumer repos (spk lint path + repo-wide pretender gate)
description: Reported from testaruda (gh-71 fix session, blocked at commit). The ddl init --gates sweep (DDL-d73, testaruda PR #72 / 41d9838) added two managed pre-commit hooks to lefthook.yml that fail even with NOTHING staged-changed: (1) ddl-spk-lint runs 'spk lint openspec' — wrong corpus path: spk doctor itself hints 'spk lint openspec/specs', but even that exits 2 'no spec files found — nothing was linted' when the consumer's specs are plain openspec format (no specodelic frontmatter). Exit 2 (nothing-to-lint) should not gate the commit until the repo adopts dual format. (2) ddl-pretender-gate runs 'pretender check --mode gate' repo-wide — fails on pre-existing violations in untouched files (tests/ordering.rs, tests/seeded_fault.rs in testaruda), blocking every commit. The pre-push pretender hook already uses --diff-only, which passes; the template should be consistent. Suggested template fix: 'spk lint openspec/specs || test $? -eq 2' (tolerate nothing-to-lint) and 'pretender check --diff-only --mode gate'. Worked around locally in testaruda lefthook.yml; the template (ddl init source) still ships the broken variants.
close_reason: PR #85 merged. Gates template: spk-lint tolerates nothing-to-lint (plain openspec repos), pre-commit pretender is --diff-only gate (consistent with pre-push). Template drift test asserts fixed commands. title: Publish only tested releases with narrowly scoped credentials
description:
## Parent
Security evaluation 2026-10-09, SEC-06; parent workspace charly/reports/security-2026-10-09.md (report commit 2a09a4c). Evidence below is self-contained for this repository.

## What to build
Publish only tested releases with narrowly scoped credentials. This slice delivers one observable protection from input through execution/storage to user-facing diagnostics.

**Evidence / baseline:** Release contents:write is workflow-wide; actions use mutable tags; publish depends on build jobs, not explicit test/security jobs; CI executes an unchecked bd archive.

**Lane:** DESIGN. **Complexity:** L.
Design/security invariants must be settled before implementation; use OpenSpec where required by the repository. This ticket authorizes remediation planning, not an unreviewed protocol break.

**Files / Systems:**
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `justfile`

## Verifiable Value Claim
**Must:** 0 violations of the acceptance criteria across all positive and negative fixtures below.
**Meter:** `just ci; actionlint .github/workflows/release.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml`. Any new meter script named here is a required implementation deliverable, not an existing passing check. Add explicit regression assertions for every criterion; an empty suite is not a pass.
**Baseline:** Release contents:write is workflow-wide; actions use mutable tags; publish depends on build jobs, not explicit test/security jobs; CI executes an unchecked bd archive.
**Regression suite:** just ci

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All third-party actions use full reviewed commit SHAs; zero build jobs have contents:write or publication credentials.
- [ ] Publishing depends on passing tests, dependency advisory and secret checks for the exact tagged commit; failed/skipped/cancelled prerequisites prevent publication.
- [ ] The bd bootstrap archive is verified before extraction/execution.
- [ ] Separate build and publication authority; document credential scopes and verify actual repository protections without assuming their absence.
- [ ] Add failing regression fixtures first, demonstrate red then green, and retain existing regression coverage.
- [ ] New source files open with Purpose / Responsibilities / Rationale; contract-changing edits update Rationale.

## Blocked by
None. DESIGN work may start; implementation waits for the documented design/approval required by repository policy.

## Workflow and anti-goals
TDD: write the failing test before implementation. Tidy First: keep behavior-preserving cleanup in a separate commit/ticket; do not combine unrelated refactoring with the fix.
Do not remove, skip or weaken assertions to obtain green results. Do not introduce unrelated dependencies or lockfile churn. Any verifier/sandbox dependency needs explicit design justification. Do not break public interfaces, output contracts or installation behavior beyond the approved security transition. Do not use real credentials or mutate live releases in tests. Do not infer a known vulnerability or live remote policy from a local snapshot.

title: DECIDE: ship openspec skills from ddl init (--tools agents --scope project, 2.1+) vs config-only (--tools none)
description:
Context: openspec >= 1.0 carries agent instructions in skills (`.agents/skills/openspec-*`), not in `AGENTS.md`. `ddl init` runs `openspec init --tools none`, so a ddl-initialized repo has no openspec agent surface beyond `openspec/config.yaml`.

## Options

- **A — keep `--tools none`.** Repo footprint unchanged; agents get no openspec workflows; doctor checks only the artifact.
- **B — `openspec init --tools agents --scope project`** (2.1+; 2.0 has no `--scope`). Agents get the workflows in the vendor-neutral folder; cost: six version-tied skill directories committed per repo, churned on every pin bump, plus `.agents/skills/.openspec-target`.

## Evidence

- 2.1 without `--scope` writes the machine-global `~/.config/agents/skills` — must never happen from ddl.
- 2.1 with `--scope project` writes `.agents/skills` in the repo.
- `openspec update` refreshes committed skills and prints "Detected new tools" noise.

## Gate

Ship B only if the committed-churn cost is accepted for all nine sweep repos; otherwise record A.

## Closing rule

Closes on the user's decision (design lane). Option B creates an implementation ticket; Option A records the rationale here and closes. No code in this ticket.
close_reason: Option B, forced (no opt-in): ddl init installs openspec project skills via 'openspec init --tools agents --scope project' on 2.1+, with a version guard that refuses unscoped/older installs. Migration is forced: project.md content moves into config.yaml. Implementation ticket follows.

title: Fleet sweep: migrate the nine legacy openspec repos (openspec update, project.md → config.yaml)
description:

## Procedure per repo (two commits)

1. `openspec update --force`
   - removes the `OPENSPEC:START` markers from `AGENTS.md` (prose preserved);
   - deletes `openspec/AGENTS.md`. Non-TTY `update` without `--force` is a no-op when that file exists — `--force` is required.
2. `openspec init --tools agents --scope project`
   - creates `openspec/{changes,config.yaml,specs}` and commits `.agents/skills/openspec-*` (6 core skills + `.openspec-target`).
   - Never run without `--scope` (2.1 unscoped writes `~/.config/agents/skills`; 2.0 has no `--scope`).
3. Migrate `openspec/project.md` into `config.yaml` (`context`, `rules`, `operations`), then delete `project.md`. Sizes: espectacular 25, whisper 45, testaruda 82, dont 87, wai 97, pretender 98, dulce-de-leche 107, vampiro 134, specodelic 181 lines.

- `git diff --stat` touches only `AGENTS.md`, `openspec/`, `.agents/skills/`.
- `AGENTS.md` contains no `OPENSPEC:START` and no `openspec/AGENTS.md` pointer.
- `openspec/AGENTS.md` and `openspec/project.md` are gone; `openspec/config.yaml` exists.
- `.agents/skills/openspec-propose/SKILL.md` exists and is committed.
- `ddl doctor --json` emits no `ddl.repo.blocks` finding.
- `just ci` green.

```sh
for r in wai dont pretender specodelic testaruda espectacular vampiro dulce-de-leche whisper; do
  ( cd "$r" \
    && ! grep -q 'OPENSPEC:START' AGENTS.md \
    && ! grep -q 'openspec/AGENTS.md' AGENTS.md \
    && test -f openspec/config.yaml \
    && test ! -e openspec/project.md \
    && test -f .agents/skills/openspec-propose/SKILL.md \

done
ddl doctor --json | jq -e '[.data.diagnostics[]|select(.check=="ddl.repo.blocks")]|length==0'
```

One `git revert` per commit per repo; pins untouched by the sweep.

No openspec pin change here (sun-4vg), no `openspec config profile` change (default core profile), no hand-editing of generated blocks.

title: openspec 1.0.0 retired the OPENSPEC managed block; ddl doctor must verify published artifacts (change: fix-agent-instrumentation-check)
description:
Investigated 2026-11-17; decision recorded. Implementation is tracked in DDL-ehu (openspec change `fix-agent-instrumentation-check`).

PREMISE CORRECTION: the `OPENSPEC:START` block was retired in openspec **1.0.0** ("The OPSX Release", PR #578 — "Config files removed: CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, AGENTS.md, project.md are no longer generated"), not 2.0.0. Every 0.x release writes it (0.23.0, the newest 0.x, verified); 1.0.0 and later write no AGENTS.md and publish `openspec/config.yaml` instead. Workflows moved to agent skills (`.agents/skills/openspec-*`); project facts moved to `config.yaml` (`context`/`rules`/`operations`).

Consequences verified against the installed CLI:
- ddl doctor's fix hint (`ddl init`) cannot produce the block on >= 1.0 — `openspec init --tools none` writes no AGENTS.md. The warning is unfixable, latent only under the 0.19 pin.
- `openspec update` removes authentic legacy blocks (fingerprint-gated; custom text survives) and prints the `project.md` -> `config.yaml` migration instructions.
- scope defect: nine repos carry the legacy block, sunshine is hybrid (`project.md` + `config.yaml`), genesis uses openspec with `project.md` and pins nothing.
- the contract is version-coupled: `tests/init_canonical.rs` skips when installed block writers drift from the pins.

Rejected options:
(a) ddl writes the block itself — two writers maintaining one region of AGENTS.md; `openspec update` deletes authentic copies.
(c) drop the requirement silently — openspec presence is still worth reporting; legacy and hybrid layouts are migration states.

Accepted: (b), concretely "verify what the tool publishes". Proposal: `openspec/changes/fix-agent-instrumentation-check` (validated `--strict`); doctor checks `openspec/config.yaml`, treats a legacy block as an advisory, and never demands the retired block.

Closure: closes when DDL-ehu lands. No code in this ticket.
close_reason: Decided (b): doctor verifies the published artifact; implementation in DDL-ehu (openspec change fix-agent-instrumentation-check)

- Linux: cargo first -> binary

Fleet-standard feedback from gently: ddl-standard compliance audit found gaps (no LICENSE, no justfile install/fmt recipes, no CHANGELOG, unchained bd hooks)
description:
Source: ddl-standard compliance audit of charly-vibes/gently (graph tool, fleet member). Gently mirrors ddl conventions where it matters — ci.yml runs 'just ci' with pinned tools + smoke dogfood, cross-platform legs, cargo-deny, .ddl/ gitignore entries, GitHub topics charly-vibes+dulce-de-leche — but the audit surfaced gaps the fleet standard should either help repos close or codify as an official checklist.

Gaps found in gently (tracked there as gently-off/go8/iad/ca0/skn/cpc/lmu/hny):
1. No LICENSE file at root while Cargo.toml declares license = "MIT" — GitHub shows no license; published crate is effectively license-less. HIGHEST severity, trivially checkable — a candidate for a ddl init/doctor check.
2. No rustfmt anywhere: no just fmt/fmt-check recipes, no rustfmt component in CI, no fmt gate in lefthook pre-commit. ddl gates fmt-check per *.rs — gently silently opted out.
3. justfile missing ddl utility recipes: install (cargo install --path .), build, build-release, run, clean, check, test-verbose, test-one, tools.
4. lefthook never chains 'bd hooks run pre-commit/pre-push' — ddl relies on this chain so beads checks keep running after lefthook replaces the shim (the DDL-0tp failure mode); gently's hooks silently skip bd checks. Also runs a pretender gate with no pretender.toml present.
5. No CHANGELOG.md, minimal README badges (only tracked-with-wai vs ddl's CI/Release/Docs/crates.io/license set).
6. No release.yml/smoke.yml workflows (only ci.yml); no mdbook.

Suggested ddl actions:
- Add a fleet-compliance doctor check set to 'ddl init --gates'/doctor: LICENSE-present-and-matches-Cargo.toml, rustfmt-gated, bd-hook-chain intact, CHANGELOG present — each gap above is mechanically detectable.
- Publish the fleet standard as a machine-readable checklist (the audit above was assembled by hand-diffing ddl's justfile/lefthook/CI against a member repo).
acceptance_criteria: ddl either (a) ships doctor/init checks for the detectable gaps (LICENSE, rustfmt gate, bd hook chain, CHANGELOG) and this issue is closed by that PR, or (b) the fleet-standard checklist is written down somewhere authoritative (docs/src/) so member-repo audits stop being hand-assembled.
notes:
Follow-up from the issue-review pass on gently's compliance batch: the LICENSE gap was upgraded from cosmetic to COPYRIGHT ISSUE. The pinned Graph::Easy 0.69 (gently's upstream) declares license: gpl — GNU GPL v2 'or any later version' (no Perl/Artistic dual-license in that distribution). As a self-declared Rust port, gently is a derivative and must ship GPL-2.0-or-later; MIT (its current Cargo.toml declaration) and Apache-2.0 (ddl's fleet standard) are both non-compliant for this codebase. gently-off was retitled and rewritten accordingly. Note for the suggested doctor checks: a 'LICENSE present and matches Cargo.toml license field' check would NOT have caught this — a fleet-relevant variant worth considering is flagging member-repo licenses that are non-compliant with their declared upstream/ports.
RESOLVED (compliance wave landed in gently): LICENSE GPL-2.0-or-later (corrected from declared-MIT — see prior note), all ddl-standard justfile recipes, rustfmt gate end-to-end (recipes + CI + lefthook), lefthook bd hook chain + pretender.toml with guidance lease, CHANGELOG.md, README badge set, release.yml + smoke.yml with actionlint meter. mdbook remains a recorded-decision item (gently-hny). One new fleet-relevant finding filed as gently's tooling ticket: pretender 0.7.0 has no baseline-adopt command, so mechanical reformats hard-block gate mode — worth a pretender upstream issue or a doctor check note.

title: Evaluate Nix/devenv as fleet install path: add nix to the toolchain story (wai way + versions.ddl.toml)
description:
Motivation (ghuntley.com/nix/ + historical pi session evidence): ddl's core promise is collapsing 'a dozen install paths, config formats, and version drifts' into one install — but today that one install is still homebrew/scoop/crates/cargo/npm, each with its own drift. Session evidence across the fleet: openspec/ddl/just/bd 'command not found' hits, brew-vs-cargo PATH precedence conflicts (wai docs 'Common Installation Issues'), bd requiring a pinned GitHub release download because no versioned homebrew-core formula exists, DDL-3av (tarballs without exec bit), MSRV drift (icu 2.3.0 needs rustc 1.88 vs pinned 1.85), flaky multi-OS matrix.

Proposal: add Nix (via devenv.sh) as a first-class install path alongside brew/scoop/crates: (1) a devenv.nix/flake in each repo declaring the ecosystem tool pins from versions.ddl.toml, consumable by humans, CI, and ephemeral agent sandboxes identically; (2) ddl detects nix and prefers the pinned flake env when present; (3) wai way gains a Nix detection in its Reproducible environments check (filed as wai-bvn7).

Decision needed first: is per-repo devenv the right granularity vs one fleet flake in this repo; and does nix go into [tools] of versions.ddl.toml as a pinned env provider.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded (per-repo devenv vs fleet flake); if adopted: devenv files + versions.ddl.toml nix entry + ddl status reports nix-env health
notes:
Rule-of-5 review corrections: (1) SCOPE: Nix has no native Windows support — fleet ships scoop (Windows), so devenv path is ADDITIVE, macOS/Linux only; scoop stays canonical on Windows; (2) process: don't adopt yet — spike first: hand-written devenv.nix in the wai repo pinning tools to versions.ddl.toml values, verify with 'devenv shell'; spike output feeds the granularity decision (per-repo devenv vs one fleet flake); (3) decisions are two independent things: granularity decision blocks adoption; nix-in-[tools] integration is downstream and optional. Assumes original request 'ddl dep' = ddl as the fleet dependency-management vehicle.
CONSTRAINT (2026-10-08): host machine is Bluefin 44 (atomic, ublue) — maintainers explicitly do not support Nix and have no plans to (ublue-os/bluefin#3606, closed; refs ublue-os/main#765). No host-level nix install. The devenv.nix/devenv.yaml files remain valuable as the declarative source of truth for environments we DO control: (1) GitHub Actions CI (nix installs fine on runners via determinate-systems/nix-installer-action), (2) agent sandboxes/containers, (3) any non-atomic machine. Local verification paths on Bluefin, in preference order: (a) devcontainer with devenv — container-first, and wai way's Reproducible environments check already passes on .devcontainer; (b) distrobox (present on host, 1.8.2) with nix+devenv inside — /var/home/sasha is bind-mounted so repos work in place; (c) CI-only verification. Decision record should pick (a) vs (b) for the local loop.
Paths (b) and (c) both executed successfully (2026-10-08): (b) local loop via distrobox container 'devenv' (quay.io/fedora/fedora:41, isolated home at ~/.dbx-homes/devenv) with nix 2.35 single-user + devenv 2.4.0 — all four repo shells resolve their tools (just, node v24.20.0, python 3.14.7). (c) CI workflows in gently/wanna/tambor/wild all green on first run (53s–1m13s, cachix devenv cache). REMAINING (this ticket stays open): granularity decision — per-repo devenv (current, proven) vs one fleet flake; and whether nix enters versions.ddl.toml [tools]. Evidence so far favors per-repo devenv + CI as the stable pattern; fleet flake only if cross-repo duplication of tool pins becomes real pain.
close_reason: PR #71/decision record merged. Per-repo devenv granularity selected; nix deferred from [tools] (additive macOS/Linux only; scoop canonical on Windows). Spike artifacts live in wai repo; drift detector qualitative. Adoption blocked on granularity decision being ratified — follow-up filed as needed.
